sections.heading: Lo que: what / the thing that
sections.body:
*Lo que* means "what" in the sense of "the thing that" — not a question: *Lo que quiero es dormir.* (What I want is to sleep.) *No entiendo lo que dices.* (I don't understand what you're saying.) *Haz lo que quieras.* (Do whatever you want.) *Todo lo que necesitas…* (Everything you need…)

It can also refer back to a whole idea: *Llegó tarde, lo que me molestó mucho.* (He arrived late, which bothered me a lot.)

sections.heading: Lo + adjective: the … thing
sections.body:
*Lo* + masculine adjective turns it into an abstract noun: *lo bueno* (the good thing), *lo malo* (the bad thing), *lo importante* (the important thing), *lo mejor / lo peor* (the best / worst part), *lo difícil*, *lo mismo* (the same thing), *lo único* (the only thing).

*Lo bueno es que no llueve.* (The good thing is that it's not raining.) *Lo mejor del viaje fue la comida.* *Quiero lo mismo.* (I want the same.)

sections.heading: Eso, esto: pointing at ideas
sections.body: The neuter demonstratives point to ideas or situations, not things: *Eso es lo que pienso.* (That's what I think.) *Esto no me gusta nada.* (I don't like this at all.) *Por eso…* (That's why…), *Eso es.* (That's it / Exactly.) *¿Qué es eso?*

The worst part was the traffic.

Eso es lo que pienso.

Esto no me gusta nada.

¡Eso es!
That's it!
Cuéntame lo que pasó.
Tell me what happened.
